transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. Can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well… it’s not anything terribly dramatic, I don’t think. I just noticed I have this habit of getting up when everyone else is still seated—like in meetings or even at dinner. I’ll suddenly decide I need to refill my coffee, or check a handout, or walk to the back of the room, even when it’s not really urgent.

I’m not trying to be disruptive, of course. It’s just… I seem to do it enough that I thought maybe I should ask someone about it. Does that make sense?
When you feel the urge to get up and move around, do you also notice an internal feeling of restlessness or discomfort inside your body that makes it hard to stay still?

Yes… I think so, though I wouldn’t want to overstate it. It’s not unbearable or anything. But when I’m sitting at my desk grading essays, or sometimes in church, I’ll catch myself tapping my foot, clicking a pen, shifting in the seat… and then I realize I’m doing it and sort of tell myself, “Come on, settle down.”

It’s more like a little buzzing or discomfort, I suppose—like my body wants to be doing something even if I know I should just sit still. Does that answer what you mean?
Are you currently taking, or have you recently started, any antipsychotic medication or other prescription drug that affects dopamine, such as for nausea or mood?

I don’t think so, no. I’m not aware of taking anything like that—certainly nothing that was described to me as affecting dopamine.

I mean, I do take prescriptions like most people my age, but not for nausea or mood in that way, as far as I know. Should I bring a medication list next time, just to be sure?
Thinking back, did you notice this same kind of restlessness or need to move around when you were a child or teenager, or is this something that started more recently in adulthood?

I think it’s been there a long time, yes. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was—I did well in school, generally—but even as a girl, my report cards would say things like I was bright, but I had trouble staying in my seat or waiting my turn.

My mother used to tease me that I’d worn a little path between my desk and the pencil sharpener before I was even ten. So… I suppose it isn’t really new, is it?
Aside from the restlessness, do you often find it hard to stay focused on tasks, lose track of what you're doing, or forget things like appointments or where you put items?

Not especially, no… at least not in a way that I’ve thought of as a real problem. I mean, I have ordinary moments where I walk into a room and forget why, or misplace my glasses, but I assumed that was fairly normal.

With work, I’ve generally managed to keep on top of things. I wouldn’t want to say I never get distracted, but I haven’t really noticed it as the main issue. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

Would you say this restlessness or urge to move around has caused any noticeable problems—like tension with coworkers, family, or friends—in more than one area of your life, such as both at work and at home?

Yes… I suppose it has, a bit. I don’t want to overstate it, because people are generally kind, but at work in meetings I can tell some colleagues lose patience with me if I’m fidgeting or getting up too much.

And it’s happened in my book club as well—just that feeling that I’m annoying people or making them uncomfortable. I usually leave feeling embarrassed, rather than feeling like I’ve connected with everyone. Does that count as the sort of problem you mean?
